key_insight: An internally developed hand-keypoint detection pipeline achieved 85.9% accuracy on browser-recorded surgical training videos versus 81.5% on overhead recordings.
clinical_relevance: Browser-based video could make automated surgical skill assessment more accessible without specialized recording hardware, though skill-assessment validity was not established.
method: Retrospective technical validation of videos from 14 PGY-1 interns at one academic center.
Annotated 203 frames with 6,232 ground-truth hand keypoints across browser-based and overhead recordings.
Compared an internal pipeline with MediaPipe Hands using keypoint localization accuracy and detection rates.
evidence_signal: Anatomically normalized percentage of correct keypoints was 85.9% (95% CI, 80.3–91.0) for browser recordings and 81.5% (76.7–87.0) for overhead recordings; internal-pipeline detection rates were 94.9% and 97.7%, respectively.
watch_item: The small, single-center technical validation does not establish generalizability or demonstrate accurate assessment of surgical skill.
paper_title: Browser-Based Video Supports Scalable Computer Vision Analysis for Open Surgical Skill Assessment
